newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain sees inflation on track to two pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain sees inflation on track to two pct.

text.p: The Bank of Spain said on Friday that the current inflation trend should ensure its 1998-target of close to two percent inflation should be met.
It added that 1996 gross domestic product did not point to inflationary pressures in the short run, but added it would stick to a vigilant monetary policy to ensure foreign exchange stability.

The moderation in Spanish inflation to 2.5 percent year-on-year in February "put the Spanish economy in a favourable situation to meet the planned medium-term goal," the Bank of Spain wrote in its latest report.
The Bank of Spain stressed, however, the importance of a stable peseta.
The report said excessive peseta volatility in the coming months could prompt the central bank to "preserve the monetary stability in order to back the forex stability".

The commitment of monetary policy toward sustained inflation stability in the medium-term, in line with the most competitive European economies, "has already been largely met but still remains vulnerable to certain risks which should be prevented".

The 4.4 percent ratio of public deficit over the gross domestic product reached in 1996 was "a relevant factor when markets were evaluating Spain's probability of entering the European Monetary Union as scheduled," the central bank wrote.

The Bank of Spain said in order to maintain moderate growth with low inflation, it was necessary to see further signs of recovery in the European economies and an improvement in the competitiveness of Spain's economy.
Further lowering of public spending is also needed "to secure the sustainability of fiscal consolidation," the report said.
